title: Two Ways to Build a World · Why read this book?

narrator.label: Narrator
narrator.description: An articulate adult English narrator with warm authority and a thoughtful, varied cadence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A nearly forty-year-old idea claims societies keep organizing around partnership or domination.

direction.delivery: Open with quiet weight, let 'partnership or domination' land as the stakes.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Two Ways to Build a World keeps Riane Eisler's contrast and drops the peaceful golden age.

direction.delivery: Plain and fair, a small turn on 'drops'.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It treats domination and partnership as two recurring ways people coordinate under power.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its central claim is that technology and institutions change which way is cheaper.

direction.delivery: Lean in slightly on 'technology and institutions' and 'cheaper'.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Instead of labelling whole civilizations, the book measures relationships along distinct dimensions.

direction.delivery: Measured and clear, as if laying out a map.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It asks who can leave, speak, appeal, observe decisions, and impose sanctions.

direction.delivery: Brisk list, a short beat between each verb.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Domination appears when wealth, media, office, and force convert into each other until escape disappears.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Hierarchy can stay legitimate when its purpose, scope, duration, review, and exit are clear.

direction.delivery: Warmer and calm, release the tension.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Drawing on commons governance, it shows cooperation needs boundaries, monitoring, graduated sanctions, and appeal.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Artificial intelligence can become an empire machine, or it can lower the cost of partnership.

direction.delivery: Contrast the two halves, slight pause before 'or'.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Start with Chapter 3, From Binary to Coordinate System, and learn to map who holds power.

direction.delivery: Friendly and direct, name the chapter clearly, warm lift on 'who holds power'.
